name: Coaching Without Writing
title: Coaching Without Writing
answer: Coaching without writing means using AI to ask questions, challenge thinking and help a student plan, while the student writes every sentence they turn in. It matters because the tool can support the thinking behind an essay without doing the writing for the student. The book presents this as a sensible practice, not a proven one, because no trial has yet tested this design for essay writing.

crumbs.name: Reading and Writing, Kindergarten Through 12th Grade

sections.body: Some of the most useful AI support in writing never appears in the final piece. A school can set up an outline coach that asks questions instead of drafting, so a student works out what they want to argue and how to arrange it. With a school account in a tool such as Gemini for Education, a teacher can write standing instructions that tell the tool never to draft paragraphs. The student then leaves with a plan written in their own words. The problem this solves is that AI can easily replace the thinking a writing assignment is meant to build, while this design keeps the intellectual work with the student.
sections.heading: The idea

sections.body: In the classroom, the teacher sets up the tool so it asks questions rather than produces prose, and the student uses that questioning to build an outline or plan in their own words. For older students, the text describes a debate partner approach: a student preparing an argument can ask a configured tool to raise the strongest objections to their position, then practice answering them. This works well for students 13 and older using tools approved for their age. Across grade bands, the student's job is to respond with evidence, and the teacher reviews the final argument. The text does not give separate routines for each grade band beyond the older student debate partner and the general outline coach.
sections.heading: How it works in school

sections.body: The book labels this idea as practice rather than research for writing. It points to research outside writing: in math and computer programming trials, tools that gave hints protected learning, while tools that gave full answers raised practice scores but not learning (Bastani et al., 2025; Bassner et al., 2026). No trial has yet tested the same design for essay writing, so schools should treat it as a sensible practice rather than a proven one. The logic still applies because the student has to do the thinking.
sections.heading: What the evidence says

sections.body: The main limit is that the evidence for essay writing is not yet there, so this should not be presented as a proven method. The tool must be configured so it never drafts paragraphs, and the student must leave with a plan in their own words. For older students, the text says to use tools approved for their age, and the student's job is to respond with evidence. The teacher reviews the final argument, so the judgment about whether the argument holds stays with a person. The decisions about setup, age approval and final review remain with the teacher and school, not the AI.
